title: Kissing Bridge Trailway pedestrian bridge over Conestogo River
subtitle: Two roundabout expropriations, Grand River Transit ridership growth, and a staff report on provincial funding.
overview: The committee's main business was a proposed pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River at Wallenstein on the Kissing Bridge Trailway. Today, trail users must detour along Line 86, which was described as dangerous because of heavy traffic. The committee recommended that Council direct staff to prioritize analysis of the bridge, reuse engineering and environmental work already done, and apply for provincial funding, with possible construction in 2025 {{vote:m3}}. The motion does not commit the Region to funding the project.

The committee also recommended two follow-up reports: a funding report for the September 25 Council meeting, and a report on costs and timelines for the committee on November 5 {{vote:m2}}. This matters because the project is not in the Region's capital forecast, and the Region, as lease holder, would take on long-term maintenance liability.

The consent agenda was also approved, including expropriations of land for roundabouts at Fischer Hallman Road and New Dundee Road, and at Roseville Road and Edworthy Side Road. The committee received a Grand River Transit report showing continued ridership growth, and a councillor clarified a provincial funding deadline under other business.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council direct staff to prioritize design and construction analysis for the Conestogo River bridge, with possible construction in 2025, work with local partners on options including a 2.4 metre width, apply for provincial funding, and consider a consultant or short-term contract rather than a new full-time employee.
The committee recommended that staff report to the committee on November 5 with cost breakdowns and timelines, and report on provincial funding at the September 25 Council meeting.

decisions.item: Fischer Hallman and New Dundee roundabout expropriation
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve expropriating partial takings and temporary grading easements in Kitchener and North Dumfries for the roundabout at Fischer Hallman Road and New Dundee Road.
The committee recommended that Council approve expropriating partial takings and temporary grading easements in North Dumfries for the roundabout at Roseville Road and Edworthy Side Road.

debate: A delegate supporting the bridge said the Line 86 detour is dangerous and the project is ready to proceed. Fundraising cannot start until the Region signals support, and private funding and federal money could be lost if the project is delayed.

One councillor said the motion is not a true green light, because the project is not in the capital forecast, cost and delivery responsibility are unclear, and 2025 construction looked unlikely. The same councillor asked whether staff could be guided to study a narrower 2.4 metre width.

Staff said the project is not in the transportation plan because it is mainly recreational. A bridge with in-river work would likely need a Schedule B environmental assessment, and the delegate's cost estimates exclude temporary in-river works. Staff also said an assessment could push construction to 2027.

Councillors asked who decides the level of environmental assessment and Indigenous consultation. One asked whether Wellesley Township could lead and apply for funding. Staff replied that the Region holds the lease and would have to apply, in partnership with the township, and would take on long-term maintenance liability.

On the transit report, one councillor asked whether boardings per hour fairly measures long rural routes. Staff said it shows popularity, not cost efficiency, and that a township transit strategy is looking at on-demand and circulator services. Other councillors asked for service in specific growing areas.
